reason: The rough edge is described as breaking the skin and a blood vessel, so it should establish the injury that needs clotting.
expectation: The body will have a small cut and a damaged blood vessel.

effect: The injury is established, with the damaged vessel already narrowed; platelets are the next plausible step in stopping the bleeding.
reaction: The narrowed vessel makes the initial response visible.
reason: Platelets at the cut should gather at the damaged vessel and begin forming a plug.
expectation: Platelets will adhere at the cut and help limit bleeding.

effect: The platelet plug slows the leak; fibrin is a plausible next reinforcement.
reaction: The distinction between slowing the leak and securing it is useful.
reason: Activated clotting factors should convert soluble fibrinogen into fibrin for the clot.
expectation: Fibrinogen will be converted into fibrin that can reinforce the platelet plug.

effect: The clotting factors produced fibrin threads, which can now be added to the platelet plug.
reaction: The thread mesh makes the reinforcement easy to picture.
reason: Fibrin threads should reinforce the platelet plug at the vessel break.
expectation: A reinforced clot will limit the bleeding.

effect: The fibrin mesh reinforces the platelet plug and stops the bleeding, while the skin remains open; the chapter is complete without showing tissue repair.
reaction: The distinction between a sealed vessel and an unclosed skin cut is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Reinforcing the platelet plug with fibrin was most worthwhile: the planned cutaway distinguishes stopping bleeding from closing the skin.

leastWorthwhile.text: Creating the cut was straightforward and offered less explanation than the clotting steps, though it established the problem clearly.

surprise.text: The damaged vessel was already narrowed when the cut appeared, before platelets were added; the result did not explain that response.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the conversion of fibrinogen into threads was presented without explaining how the activated clotting factors cause it.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the still-open skin heals, since stopping bleeding leaves that question unresolved.
